gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Sony MEX-N5300BT, at $158, is the cheapest CD receiver in the set with three pairs of 4-volt preamp outputs (front, rear and a dedicated sub) plus a two-phone Bluetooth connection, while ChatGPT's 'best all-around' JVC KD-T920BTS costs more ($179) and has only two pairs of 2.5-volt preamp outputs.
standout_why: Crutchfield's 'Best Car Stereos for 2026' (the only page ChatGPT cited) returned 403 to both of my fetches, so I could not check it and it may already say this. I did read World Wide Stereo's 'Best Car Stereos of 2026', updated 2026-08-28. It names the MEX-N5300BT and KDC-X705 as CD receivers but shows no prices for them and gives no preamp counts or voltages. ChatGPT's search results 1–14 are single-product pages for the DEH-S4220BT, KD-T920BTS and KDC-BT370U. None of them sets preamp outputs and price side by side across the whole CD-receiver set.
decides: This confirms the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT ($149.99 at Abt and Sonic Electronix) as the cheapest pick if you just want CD and Bluetooth. For anyone who may add an amp or subwoofer, or who shares the car with a second phone, the Sony MEX-N5300BT ($158) has more for less money. It beats ChatGPT's 'best all-around' JVC KD-T920BTS ($179), which loses on preamp voltage (2.5 V vs 4 V) and preamp count (2 pairs vs 3). The Pioneer FH-S722BS ($229.99) loses on price, and it is out of stock at Sonic Electronix. Kenwood's KDC-X305 at Abt now costs $219, not the $199 ChatGPT showed.
